section.content: A machine learning device. Provided is a technique capable of predicting the deformation of a three-dimensional shaped object during production. The machine learning device is provided with: a data acquisition unit that acquires first data including shape data relating to a target shape of a three-dimensional object and molding condition data relating to conditions under which the three-dimensional object is molded by a three-dimensional molding device, and second data relating to deformation of the three-dimensional object; a storage unit that stores a learning data set including a plurality of first data and a plurality of second data; and a learning unit that learns the relationship between the first data and the second data by performing machine learning using the learning data set.

一种机器学习装置。提供一种能够预测在制造时的三维造型物的变形的技术。机器学习装置具备：数据获取部，获取第一数据和第二数据，该第一数据包含与三维造型物的目标形状相关的形状数据以及与由三维造型装置对三维造型物进行造型时的条件相关的造型条件数据，该第二数据与三维造型物的变形相关；存储部，存储包含多个第一数据和多个第二数据的学习数据集；以及学习部，通过执行使用了学习数据集的机器学习，来学习第一数据与第二数据的关系。

Machine learning deviceTechnical Field

The present disclosure relates to a machine learning device.

Background

There is known a technique of forming a three-dimensional shaped object by laminating materials including powdered metal and ceramic, and then sintering the three-dimensional shaped object to improve strength. Since the three-dimensional shaped object shrinks by sintering, strain, cracks, warpage, and the like may occur in the three-dimensional shaped object after sintering. Regarding this problem, patent document 1 describes the following technique: the amount of deformation of the three-dimensional shaped object due to heat is predicted using a finite element method, and when the predicted amount of deformation is not within an allowable range, the input geometry is corrected, and the three-dimensional shaped object is shaped based on the corrected input geometry, thereby suppressing deformation of the three-dimensional shaped object.

Patent document 1: japanese Kohyo publication No. 2017-530027

The amount of deformation of the three-dimensional shaped object due to the heat treatment depends on, for example, the shape, thickness, and material of the three-dimensional shaped object, or a combination of various conditions such as the temperature, temperature rise rate, and time of the heat treatment on the three-dimensional shaped object. Therefore, in the technique of predicting the amount of deformation of the three-dimensional shaped object by using the finite element method as in patent document 1, it is difficult to accurately predict the amount of deformation. Such a problem is not limited to the case of manufacturing a three-dimensional shaped object by stacking powdered metals and the like and then sintering them, but is also a common problem in the case of manufacturing a three-dimensional shaped object by stacking plasticized thermoplastic resins.

Disclosure of Invention

According to one aspect of the present disclosure, a machine learning device is provided. The machine learning device includes: a data acquisition unit that acquires first data including shape data relating to a target shape of a three-dimensional object and first data relating to molding condition data relating to molding conditions under which the three-dimensional object is molded by a three-dimensional molding device, and second data relating to deformation of the three-dimensional object; a storage unit that stores a learning data set including a plurality of the first data and a plurality of the second data; and a learning unit that learns a relationship between the first data and the second data by performing machine learning using the learning data set.

Detailed Description

A. The first embodiment:

fig. 1 is an explanatory diagram showing a schematic configuration of a machine learning system 50 according to a first embodiment. The machine learning system 50 includes: a machine learning device 100, an information processing device 200, a three-dimensional modeling device 300, a heat treatment device 400, and an inspection device 500.

The machine learning device 100 is configured by a computer including one or more processors, a main storage device, and an input/output interface that inputs and outputs signals to and from the outside. In the present embodiment, the machine learning device 100 generates a learning model by executing a learning process described later, predicts a manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object using the learning model by executing a prediction process described later, and executes a correction process described later when the predicted manufacturing error is not within an allowable range. The machine learning apparatus 100 may be configured by a plurality of computers.

In the present embodiment, the machine learning device 100 includes: the data acquisition unit 110, the data storage unit 120, the calculation unit 130, the preprocessing unit 140, the learning unit 150, the learning model storage unit 160, the prediction unit 170, the correction unit 180, and the correction function storage unit 190.

The data acquisition unit 110 acquires the first data from the information processing apparatus 200, the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300, and the heat treatment apparatus 400 by wired communication or wireless communication. The first data includes shape data and modeling data, which will be described later. Further, the data acquisition unit 110 acquires the second data from the inspection apparatus 500 by wired communication or wireless communication. The second data includes measurement data described later.

The data storage unit 120 stores various data such as first data and second data. The arithmetic unit 130 generates manufacturing error data, which will be described later, using the shape data included in the first data and the measurement data included in the second data. The preprocessing unit 140 generates a learning data set using the first data and the manufacturing error data. In the learning process, the learning unit 150 executes machine learning using the learning data set to generate a learning model. In the present embodiment, the learning unit 150 includes a reward calculation unit 151 and a cost function update unit 152. The learning model storage unit 160 stores a learning model. The prediction unit 170 predicts a manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object by using the learning model in the prediction process. In the prediction process, the correction unit 180 corrects the modeling data included in the first data based on the prediction result of the prediction unit 170. The correction function storage unit 190 stores a correction function for correcting the modeling data by the correction unit 180.

The information processing apparatus 200 is configured by a computer including one or more processors, a main storage device, and an input/output interface for inputting and outputting signals to and from the outside. An input device such as a mouse or a keyboard, and a display device such as a liquid crystal display are connected to the information processing device 200. In the present embodiment, the information processing apparatus 200 generates shape data by three-dimensional CAD software installed in advance. The shape data represents a target shape of the three-dimensional shaped object. The target shape is a shape that is a target in manufacturing a three-dimensional shaped object. That is, when a three-dimensional shaped object is manufactured in accordance with a target shape, the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object is zero. The shape data is transmitted to the machine learning device 100. In the present embodiment, the information processing device 200 reads the shape data with the slicing software installed in advance to generate the modeling data. The modeling data is data indicating modeling conditions for modeling the three-dimensional object by the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300, that is, various information for controlling the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300. The modeling data is transmitted to the machine learning device 100 and the three-dimensional modeling device 300. The molding data may be referred to as molding condition data.

The three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300 models the three-dimensional modeled object based on the modeling data. In the present embodiment, the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300 is a paste ink-jet type three-dimensional modeling apparatus that uses an ink-jet technique to jet a pasty liquid obtained by mixing a powder material, a solvent, and a binder to model a three-dimensional modeled object. The structure of the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300 will be described later.

The heat treatment apparatus 400 performs heat treatment on the three-dimensional shaped object shaped by the three-dimensional shaping apparatus 300. In the present embodiment, the heat treatment apparatus 400 is a sintering furnace. The heat treatment apparatus 400 sinters the three-dimensional shaped object under predetermined heat treatment conditions. The three-dimensional shaped object shrinks through sintering, and the strength of the three-dimensional shaped object is improved. The heat treatment conditions include, for example, heating time, heating temperature, heating rate, and the number of times of heating in the heat treatment step.

The inspection apparatus 500 measures the dimensions of the three-dimensional shaped object after the heat treatment, and generates measurement data. In the present embodiment, the inspection apparatus 500 is a three-dimensional measuring machine. In the present embodiment, the measurement data represents the shape of the three-dimensional shaped object after the heat treatment. The measurement data may indicate the amount of deformation, the amount of warpage, the presence or absence of cracks, and the like of the three-dimensional shaped object after the heat treatment.

Fig. 2 is an explanatory diagram showing a schematic configuration of the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300. The three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300 includes a control unit 301, a table unit 302, a moving mechanism 303, and a modeling unit 304. The control unit 301 is configured by a computer including one or more processors, a main storage device, and an input/output interface for inputting and outputting signals to and from the outside. The control unit 301 controls the table unit 302, the moving mechanism 303, and the modeling unit 304 based on the modeling data supplied from the information processing apparatus 200.

The table unit 302 includes a table 310 and an elevating mechanism 316 for moving the table 310 in the Z direction. In the present embodiment, the lifting mechanism 316 is composed of an actuator that moves the table 310 in the Z direction under the control of the control unit 301.

The moving mechanism 303 is provided above the table unit 302. The moving mechanism 303 supports the modeling unit 304, and moves the modeling unit 304 relative to the table 310 in the X direction. In the present embodiment, the moving mechanism 303 is constituted by an actuator that moves the modeling unit 304 in the X direction under the control of the control unit 301.

The modeling unit 304 is disposed above the table unit 302. The molding unit 304 includes a first material supply unit 320, a second material supply unit 330, and a curing energy supply unit 350. In the modeling unit 304, a first material supply unit 320, a second material supply unit 330, and a solidification energy supply unit 350 are arranged in this order from the-X direction side.

The first material supply unit 320 supplies a first liquid LQ1, which is a pasty liquid containing a powder material, a solvent, and a binder, onto the table 310. The first material supply unit 320 includes a first supply source 321 as a supply source of the first liquid LQ1, and a first head 322 that supplies the first liquid LQ1 to the table 310. In the present embodiment, the first supply source 321 is constituted by a tank that stores the first liquid LQ 1. The first head 322 is constituted by a liquid ejecting head of a piezoelectric driving method including: the piezoelectric element includes a pressure chamber, a piezoelectric element for changing a volume of the pressure chamber, and a plurality of nozzle holes communicating with the pressure chamber. A plurality of nozzle holes are provided along the Y direction in the first head 322. In the first head 322, the piezoelectric element deflects the side wall of the pressure chamber filled with the first liquid LQ1 supplied from the first supply source 321 to reduce the volume of the pressure chamber, and the first liquid LQ1 is ejected from the nozzle holes in an amount corresponding to the reduction in the volume of the pressure chamber.

The second material supply unit 330 supplies a second liquid LQ2, which is a pasty liquid containing a powder material, a solvent, and a binder, to the table 310. The second material supply unit 330 includes a second supply source 331 as a supply source of the second liquid LQ2, and a second head 332 for supplying the second liquid LQ2 onto the table 310. In the present embodiment, the second supply source 331 is constituted by a tank storing the second liquid LQ 2. The second head 332 is configured by a liquid ejecting head of a piezoelectric driving method including: the piezoelectric element includes a pressure chamber, a piezoelectric element for changing a volume of the pressure chamber, and a plurality of nozzle holes communicating with the pressure chamber. A plurality of nozzle holes are provided in the second head 332 along the Y direction. In the second head 332, the piezoelectric element deflects the side wall of the pressure chamber filled with the second liquid LQ2 supplied from the second supply source 331 to reduce the volume of the pressure chamber, and the second liquid LQ2 corresponding to the amount of reduction in the volume of the pressure chamber is ejected from the nozzle holes.

The powder material contained in the first liquid LQ1 and the second liquid LQ2 is a raw material of the three-dimensional shaped object. Examples of the powder material include powders of metal materials such as stainless steel, steel other than stainless steel, pure iron, titanium alloy, magnesium alloy, cobalt alloy, and nickel alloy, and powders of ceramic materials such as silica, titania, alumina, zirconia, and silicon nitride. One of them may be used as a powder material, or two or more of them may be used in combination as a powder material. In the present embodiment, stainless steel powder is used as the powder material contained in the first liquid LQ1 and the second liquid LQ 2.

Examples of the solvent contained in the first liquid LQ1 and the second liquid LQ2 include water, alkylene glycol monoalkyl ethers such as ethylene glycol monomethyl ether, acetic acid esters such as ethyl acetate, aromatic hydrocarbons such as benzene, ketones such as methyl ethyl ketone, and alcohols such as ethanol. One of them may be used as a solvent, or two or more of them may be used in combination as a solvent.

As the binder included in the first liquid LQ1 and the second liquid LQ2, various photocurable resins such as a thermoplastic resin, a thermosetting resin, a visible light curable resin that cures with light in the visible light region, an ultraviolet curable resin, and an infrared curable resin, an X-ray curable resin, and the like can be used. One of them may be used as a binder, or two or more of them may be used in combination as a binder. In the present embodiment, a thermosetting resin is used as a binder included in the first liquid LQ1 and the second liquid LQ 2.

The particle density of the first liquid LQ1 is lower than that of the second liquid LQ 2. Particle density refers to the volume of powder material per unit volume. By reducing the number of particles of the powder material per unit volume in each of the liquids LQ1, LQ2, the particle density of each of the liquids LQ1, LQ2 can be reduced. The particle density of each of the liquids LQ1 and LQ2 can also be reduced by increasing the average particle diameter of the powder material contained in each of the liquids LQ1 and LQ 2. As the average particle diameter, for example, a median particle diameter can be used. In the present embodiment, the number of particles of the powder material per unit volume in the first liquid LQ1 is smaller than the number of particles of the powder material per unit volume in the second liquid LQ 2. The average particle diameter of the powder material contained in the first liquid LQ1 is the same as the average particle diameter of the powder material contained in the second liquid LQ 2.

The curing energy supply unit 350 applies energy for curing the binder contained in the first liquid LQ1 and the second liquid LQ 2. In the present embodiment, the curing energy supply unit 350 is constituted by a heater. The solvents contained in the first liquid LQ1 and the second liquid LQ2 supplied to the stage 310 are volatilized by heating from the curing energy supply unit 350, and the binder contained in the first liquid LQ1 and the second liquid LQ2 supplied to the stage 310 is cured by heating from the curing energy supply unit 350. When an ultraviolet-curable bonding material is used, the curing energy supply unit 350 may be an ultraviolet lamp.

Fig. 3 is an explanatory diagram schematically showing a state in which the target shape of the three-dimensional object OB is divided into a plurality of layers. Fig. 4 is an explanatory diagram schematically showing a case where a layer of the three-dimensional object OB is divided into a plurality of voxels VX. In the present embodiment, the target shape of the three-dimensional shaped object OB indicated by the shape data is divided into a plurality of layers having a predetermined thickness by slicing software while enlarging the size in consideration of the shrinkage rate by the heat treatment. Fig. 3 shows, as an example, a case where the target shape of the three-dimensional object OB is divided into 7 layers. Each layer is referred to as a first layer LY1, a second layer LY2, a third layer LY3, a fourth layer LY4, a fifth layer LY5, a sixth layer LY6, and a seventh layer LY7 in this order from the-Z direction side. In the present embodiment, each layer is divided into a plurality of voxels VX in a cubic or rectangular parallelepiped shape having a predetermined volume by slicing software. Fig. 4 shows an example in which the fourth layer LY4 is divided into a plurality of voxels VX.

The modeling data includes information on the position of each voxel VX and information on the type of liquid used to model each voxel VX. In the example shown in fig. 4, the second liquid LQ2 is used to shape each voxel VX in the region surrounded by the two-dot chain line in the fourth layer LY4, and the first liquid LQ1 is used to shape each voxel VX other than this. In the following description, a portion of the three-dimensional object OB to be molded using the first liquid LQ1 will be referred to as a first portion P1, and a portion of the three-dimensional object OB to be molded using the second liquid LQ2 will be referred to as a second portion P2.

Fig. 5 is a flowchart showing a method for producing the three-dimensional object OB according to the present embodiment. A method for producing the three-dimensional object OB will be described by taking a case of producing the three-dimensional object OB shown in fig. 3 and 4 as an example. First, in the modeling data acquisition step of step S110, the control unit 301 of the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300 acquires modeling data from the information processing apparatus 200.

In the molding step of step S120, as shown in fig. 2, the control unit 301 controls the molding unit 304, the moving mechanism 303, and the lifting mechanism 316 of the table unit 302 based on the molding data, thereby molding the three-dimensional object OB on the table 310. In the initial state, the modeling unit 304 is disposed on the + X direction side of the table 310. The controller 301 controls the moving mechanism 303 to move the modeling unit 304 in the-X direction. The controller 301 controls the first material supplier 320 to supply the first liquid LQ1 to the position where the first portion P1 is to be molded while moving the molding unit 304 in the-X direction, controls the second material supplier 330 to supply the second liquid LQ2 to the position where the second portion P2 is to be molded, and controls the curing energy supplier 350 to cure the binder contained in the liquids LQ1 and LQ2 supplied to the table 310. The nth layer of the three-dimensional shaped object OB is formed by curing the binder. n is an arbitrary natural number. Thereafter, the controller 301 controls the moving mechanism 303 to return the modeling unit 304 to the position on the + X direction side of the table 310, and controls the lifting mechanism 316 to lower the table 310 by the thickness of the nth layer. The controller 301 repeats the above-described process to stack the (n + 1) th layer on the nth layer, thereby forming the three-dimensional object OB.

In the heat treatment step of step S130 in fig. 5, the three-dimensional shaped object OB is subjected to heat treatment. In the present embodiment, the heat treatment apparatus 400 heats the three-dimensional shaped object OB under predetermined heat treatment conditions, thereby degreasing the binder from the three-dimensional shaped object OB and sintering the three-dimensional shaped object OB. The sintering shrinks the three-dimensional object OB, thereby improving the strength of the three-dimensional object OB.

In the inspection step of step S140, the inspection device 500 measures the size of the three-dimensional shaped object OB after the heat treatment step, and generates measurement data. The measurement data is transmitted to the machine learning device 100. After the inspection step of step S140, the method of manufacturing the three-dimensional object OB is ended.

Fig. 6 is a perspective view showing an example of the three-dimensional object OB after the heat treatment step. The heat treatment step shrinks the three-dimensional shaped object OB. In the three-dimensional shaped object OB, a portion having a relatively high shrinkage rate and a portion having a relatively low shrinkage rate may occur. Since a large difference occurs in the shrinkage rate in the three-dimensional shaped object OB, strain, warpage, cracks, and the like may occur in the three-dimensional shaped object OB. The three-dimensional shaped object OB shown in fig. 6 has a first surface PL1, a second surface PL2, a third surface PL3, a fourth surface PL4, a fifth surface PL5, a sixth surface PL6, a seventh surface PL7, and an eighth surface PL 8. In this example, since the shrinkage rates of the second face PL2 and the sixth face PL6 are relatively high, the second face PL2 and the sixth face PL6 generate strain. In response to such a problem, by adjusting the distribution of the particle density in the three-dimensional shaped object OB, the occurrence of strain, warpage, and cracks in the three-dimensional shaped object OB can be suppressed. For example, by increasing the particle density of a portion having a relatively high shrinkage ratio, the shrinkage ratio of the portion can be reduced, and by decreasing the particle density of a portion having a relatively low shrinkage ratio, the shrinkage ratio of the portion can be increased. That is, by adjusting the arrangement of the first portion P1 molded using the first liquid LQ1 and the second portion P2 molded using the second liquid LQ2 in the three-dimensional object OB, the occurrence of strain, warpage, and cracks in the three-dimensional object OB can be suppressed.

Fig. 7 is a flowchart showing the contents of the learning process in the present embodiment. This process is executed by the machine learning device 100, for example, when the production of one three-dimensional object OB is completed. First, in step S210, the data acquisition unit 110 acquires first data. The first data includes shape data relating to the target shape of the three-dimensional shaped object OB and shape data generated based on the shape data. In the present embodiment, the first data further includes heat treatment condition data indicating heat treatment conditions in the heat treatment step. The acquired first data is stored in the data storage section 120.

In step S220, the data acquisition unit 110 acquires the second data. The second data includes measurement data generated in the inspection process. In the present embodiment, the measurement data indicates the shape of the three-dimensional shaped object OB after the heat treatment step. The acquired second data is stored in the data storage section 120 in association with the corresponding first data. The order of the processing in step S210 and the processing in step S220 may be reversed.

In step S230, the arithmetic unit 130 reads the shape data included in the first data and the measurement data included in the second data stored in the data storage unit 120, and generates manufacturing error data indicating an error between the size of the shape of the three-dimensional shaped object OB after the heat treatment process and the size of the target shape. The generated manufacturing error data is stored in the data storage unit 120 in association with the corresponding first data. In step S240, the preprocessing unit 140 reads the first data stored in the data storage unit 120 and the manufacturing error data associated with the first data, and generates a learning data set.

In step S250, the learning unit 150 reads the learning data set generated by the preprocessing unit 140, and executes machine learning to generate a learning model. In step S260, the learning model storage unit 160 stores the learning model generated by the learning unit 150. After that, the machine learning device 100 ends the processing. For example, each time the production of one three-dimensional object OB is completed, the machine learning device 100 repeats this process, and performs machine learning using a learning data set including data for a plurality of three-dimensional objects OB having different target shapes, modeling conditions, and heat treatment conditions, thereby updating the learning model.

The algorithm of the machine learning executed by the learning unit 150 in step S250 is not particularly limited, and for example, a known algorithm such as supervised learning, unsupervised learning, or reinforcement learning may be used. In the present embodiment, the learning unit 150 executes reinforcement learning described later. Reinforcement learning is the following method: a current state of an environment in which a learning object exists is observed, a predetermined action is executed in the current state, a cycle of giving a certain reward to the action is repeated in a trial and error manner, and a solution in which the total amount of rewards is maximized is learned as an optimal solution.

An example of an algorithm of reinforcement learning executed by the learning unit 150 will be described. The algorithm of this example is an algorithm known as Q-learning (Q-learning), and is a method of learning a function Q (s, a) indicating the action value in the case where an action a is selected in a state s, using, as independent variables, the state s of an action agent and an action a selectable by the action agent in the state s. And selecting the action a with the highest cost function Q as the optimal solution in the state s. Q learning is started in a state where the correlation between the state s and the action a is unknown, and trial and error for selecting various actions a is repeated in an arbitrary state s, whereby the cost function Q is repeatedly updated to approach the optimal solution. Here, as a result of selecting the action a in the state s, when the state s as an environment changes, the weight of the action a as the reward r corresponding to the change can be obtained, and by selecting the action a that can obtain a higher reward r through the guided learning, the cost function Q can be brought close to the optimal solution in a relatively short time.

When the learning unit 150 executes Q learning, the behavior of how the distribution of the particle density should be determined for the target shape of the three-dimensional shaped object OB in the current state, that is, how the first liquid LQ1 or the second liquid LQ2 should be supplied to the position of each voxel VX indicated by the shape data included in the first data in the current state corresponds to the action a of the update formula, and the return R obtained by the return calculation unit 151 corresponds to the return R of the update formula. Therefore, the merit function update unit 152 repeatedly updates the function Q indicating the value of the distribution of the particle density with respect to the target shape of the three-dimensional shaped object OB in the current state by Q learning using the return R.

The return R calculated by the return calculation unit 151 can obtain a positive return R when, for example, the distribution of the particle density with respect to the target shape of the three-dimensional shaped object OB is determined, when the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the determined distribution is smaller than the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the distribution before change, when the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the determined distribution is within an allowable range, or the like, when the distribution of the particle density with respect to the target shape of the three-dimensional shaped object OB is determined, when the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the determined distribution is larger than the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the distribution before change, or the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the determined distribution exceeds the allowable range, a negative reward R can be obtained.

When performing Q learning using the return R corresponding to the manufacturing error of the manufactured three-dimensional shaped object OB, the learning is guided in a direction of selecting an action that can obtain a higher return R, and the value of the action value for the action performed in the current state, that is, the function Q is updated based on the state of the environment that changes as a result of the selected action being performed in the current state, that is, the state variable S and the determination data D. By repeating this update, the function Q is rewritten to a value that is larger as the appropriate action becomes. In this way, the correlation between the current state of the unknown environment and the action thereon becomes increasingly clear.

Fig. 8 is a flowchart showing the contents of the prediction processing in the present embodiment. This process is executed by the machine learning device 100 when a predetermined start command is supplied to the machine learning device 100. First, in step S310, the data acquisition unit 110 acquires first data. The acquired first data is stored in the data storage section 120.

Next, in step S320, the prediction unit 170 reads the first data stored in the data storage unit 120 and the learning model stored in the learning model storage unit 160, predicts a manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the first data, and generates prediction result data indicating a prediction result. The prediction unit 170 can predict a manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the first data by using the value Q calculated by reading the first data and the learning model. In the present embodiment, the amount of manufacturing error is shown in the prediction result data. The prediction result data may indicate the amount of deformation, the amount of warpage, the presence or absence of cracks, and the like of the three-dimensional shaped object OB produced based on the first data. The prediction result data may also include: a symbol indicating that the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the first data is within the allowable range, and a symbol indicating that the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the first data exceeds the allowable range.

In step S330, the estimation unit 170 determines whether or not the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the first data is within an allowable range. The prediction unit 170 can determine whether or not the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the first data is within the allowable range by comparing the manufacturing error indicated by the prediction result data with a preset allowable value of the manufacturing error.

If it is not determined in step S330 that the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the first data is within the allowable range, the correction unit 180 performs a correction process of correcting the shaping data included in the first data in step S400. The correction process will be described later. Thereafter, the process returns to step S320, and the prediction unit 170 reads the first data corrected with the modeling data and the learning model, predicts the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the first data corrected with the modeling data, and generates prediction result data indicating the prediction result. The prediction unit 170 and the correction unit 180 repeat the processing of steps S400, S320, and S330 until it is determined in step S330 that the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional object OB manufactured based on the first data is within the allowable range.

If it is determined in step S330 that the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB manufactured based on the first data is within the allowable range, the machine learning device 100 outputs the shaping data and the prediction result data, and then ends the process in step S340. In the present embodiment, the machine learning device 100 outputs the modeling data and the prediction result data to the information processing device 200. In the case where the model data is corrected by the correction processing, the corrected model data and the prediction result data based on the corrected model data are output.

Fig. 9 is a flowchart showing the contents of the correction process in the present embodiment. First, in step S410, correction unit 180 reads prediction result data generated by prediction section 170. Next, in step S420, the correction unit 180 calculates the shrinkage rate of each surface of the three-dimensional object OB using the prediction result data.

In step S430, the correcting unit 180 determines whether or not the shrinkage rate of the k-th surface of the surfaces of the three-dimensional object OB is equal to or greater than a predetermined value. k is an arbitrary natural number. The correction unit 180 may compare the shrinkage rate of the k-th surface with a predetermined threshold value to determine whether or not the shrinkage rate of the k-th surface is equal to or greater than a predetermined value. When it is determined in step S430 that the shrinkage rate of the k-th surface is equal to or greater than the predetermined value, the correction unit 180 calculates a difference between the shrinkage rate of the k-th surface and the shrinkage rate of the surface opposite to the k-th surface in step S440. For example, as shown in fig. 6, when the correction process is performed on the three-dimensional object OB having 8 surfaces PL1 to PL8, the correction unit 180 determines whether or not the shrinkage rate of the first surface PL1 is equal to or greater than a predetermined value in step S430, and when determining that the shrinkage rate of the first surface PL1 is equal to or greater than a predetermined value, calculates the difference between the shrinkage rate of the first surface PL1 and the shrinkage rate of the third surface PL3 which is the surface opposite to the first surface PL1 in step S440. In step S450, the correction unit 180 reads the correction function stored in the correction function storage unit 190. In the present embodiment, the correction function is a polynomial function or a rational function. The correction function represents, for example, a relationship between the manufacturing error and a volume of the second portion P2 required to make the manufacturing error equal to or smaller than a predetermined value. The correction function may show a relationship between the warpage amount and the volume of the second portion P2 required to make the warpage amount equal to or less than a predetermined value. In step S460, the correcting unit 180 corrects the distribution of the particle density indicated by the modeling data, in other words, the information on the type of the liquid used to model each voxel VX, based on the correction function. On the other hand, if it is not determined in step S430 that the shrinkage factor of the k-th surface is equal to or greater than the predetermined value, the correction unit 180 skips the processing from step S440 to step S460.

Thereafter, in step S470, the correcting unit 180 determines whether or not the confirmation of the shrinkage rate in step S430 is performed for all the surfaces. The correction unit 180 repeats the processing from step S430 to step S470 until it is determined that the contraction rates of step S430 have been confirmed for all the surfaces. For example, in the three-dimensional shaped object OB shown in fig. 6, after the processing from step S430 to step S460 is performed on the first surface PL1, the correction unit 180 returns the processing to step S430, and determines whether or not the shrinkage rate of the second surface PL2 is equal to or greater than a predetermined value. When determining that the confirmation of the contraction rates in step S430 has been performed for all the surfaces, the correction unit 180 ends the process. Thereafter, as shown in fig. 8, the process of step S320 is performed using the corrected model data.

Fig. 10 is an explanatory diagram showing an example of the distribution of the first part P1 and the second part P2 before and after correction. After the correction shown in the lower side of fig. 10, the range of the second portion P2 molded using the second liquid LQ is expanded by changing the voxel VX molded using the first liquid LQ1 to the voxel VX molded using the second liquid LQ in the peripheral portion of the second plane PL2 and the peripheral portion of the sixth plane PL6, which are planes having a relatively large contraction rate, as compared to those before the correction shown in the upper side of fig. 10. Therefore, the variation in the shrinkage rate in the three-dimensional shaped object OB after the correction is suppressed as compared with before the correction.

According to the machine learning device 100 of the present embodiment described above, in the learning process, the learning unit 150 generates a learning model capable of predicting the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB using the learning data set generated based on the first data and the second data, and in the prediction process, the prediction unit 170 predicts whether the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB is within the allowable range using the learning model, and outputs prediction result data indicating the prediction result. In the present embodiment, when the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB predicted by the prediction unit 170 exceeds the allowable range, the correction unit 180 corrects the distribution of the particle density in the three-dimensional shaped object OB indicated by the shaping data using a correction function indicated by a polynomial function or a rational function, and outputs the shaping data after correction. Therefore, by manufacturing the three-dimensional shaped object OB using the corrected shape data, it is possible to suppress the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB from exceeding the allowable range.

In the present embodiment, the learning data set used for the generation of the learning model includes modeling data indicating the position of the first portion P1 and the position of the second portion P2 of the three-dimensional object OB, which is modeled using the first liquid LQ1, and the second portion P2 is modeled using the second liquid LQ2 having a higher particle density than the first liquid LQ 1. Therefore, a learning model capable of predicting a manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB can be generated from the distribution of the particle density in the three-dimensional shaped object OB.

In the present embodiment, the learning data set used for the generation of the learning model includes heat treatment condition data. Therefore, a learning model capable of predicting a manufacturing error of the three-dimensional shaped object OB can be generated according to the conditions of the heat treatment in the heat treatment step.

In the present embodiment, the moving mechanism 303b moves the modeling unit 304 relative to the table 310 in the X direction and the Y direction. In the present embodiment, in the molding step shown in step S120 in fig. 5, the control unit 301 controls the molding unit 304, the moving mechanism 303, and the lifting mechanism 316 of the table unit 302 based on the molding data, thereby molding the three-dimensional object OB on the table 310. The controller 301 controls the moving mechanism 303 to supply the first molten material to the position where the first part P1 is molded by controlling the first material supply unit 320b while moving the molding unit 304 in the X direction and the Y direction, and to supply the second molten material to the position where the second part P2 is molded by controlling the second material supply unit 330. The thermoplastic resin contained in the first molten material and the thermoplastic resin contained in the second molten material are cooled and solidified on the table 310, thereby forming the nth layer of the three-dimensional object OB. After that, the controller 301 lowers the table 310 by the thickness of the nth layer by controlling the lifting mechanism 316, and then repeats the above-described process to stack the (n + 1) th layer on the nth layer, thereby shaping the three-dimensional shaped object OB.

According to the machine learning system 50b of the present embodiment described above, the three-dimensional shaped object OB is shaped by the three-dimensional shaping device 300b of the FDM method. In the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300b of the FDM method, the particle density of the first molten material can be made higher than the particle density of the first liquid LQ1 of the first embodiment, and the particle density of the second molten material can be made higher than the particle density of the second liquid LQ2 of the first embodiment. Therefore, the shrinkage rate of the entire three-dimensional object OB can be made smaller than that in the first embodiment, and the three-dimensional object OB can be molded with higher dimensional accuracy.
